findings.title: Add an opt-in JSON-lines file sink for the full ILogger stream at the per-user metadata-store root
findings.description: All operational logging is stderr-only prose; the structured JSON sink fires only for unexpected exceptions and defaults to Disabled. When the server runs under an MCP host in a consumer session, stderr is captured (or dropped) by the host and no rg/jq/tail-reachable telemetry exists. HostProcessMetadataStore already resolves a per-user, XDG-aware LOCALAPPDATA root the sink can reuse. PR #1253 deliberately retired MCP protocol logging (ADR 0003) — the fix must stay on the operator-side sink path.
acceptance: An env-gated file sink writes JSON-lines records (ts UTC ISO-8601 ms, level, category, eventId, message, correlationId when present) for the full ILogger stream under the metadata-store per-user root
Default remains off; enabling requires no rebuild; stderr behavior unchanged
Foreign-CWD launch writes nothing into the working directory (existing behavior preserved)
findings.suggested_approach: Extend ServerObservabilitySinkKind vocabulary (disabled|stderr|file) or add a dedicated ROSLYNMCP_LOG_FILE toggle; register an ILoggerProvider writing JSON lines to <metadata-store-root>/logs/; reuse HostProcessMetadataStore root resolution.
findings.counterargument: The host (Claude Code) already persists MCP stderr in its own log files, so a second sink is redundant plumbing. Cost: a new file surface to rotate and document. Rebuttal: host log locations are host-specific, undocumented for agents, prose-format, and absent on other MCP hosts — the published-artifact context makes a host-independent sink the only reliable access path.

findings.title: Stamp correlation id, elapsed ms, and timestamps onto stream records
findings.description: RequestCorrelationContext exists but appears in exactly one log template (the failure line) — a correlation-id query over the captured stream returns 1 record, no chain. Success/completion lines carry neither correlation nor the already-measured stopwatch elapsed. The console formatter emits no timestamps at all (grep count 0 in captures). BeginScope/IncludeScopes are unused repo-wide.
acceptance: Every record emitted during a tool call carries the request correlation id (logging scope, not per-template interpolation)
Tool completion and failure templates include ElapsedMs and outcome
Console/file records carry UTC ISO-8601 timestamps with millisecond precision
findings.suggested_approach: BeginScope with the correlation id in StructuredCallToolFilter around dispatch; enable scopes + timestampFormat on the console options; add ElapsedMs to the completion/failure templates. Interacts with backlog row correlation-id-suffix-single-source (scope-stamping reduces the hand-interpolated suffix pattern it consolidates).
findings.counterargument: Scope output makes the prose stderr lines longer/noisier for humans tailing the stream. Rebuttal: humans are the second audience; the delta is one short suffix per line.

findings.title: Ship a consumer-facing observability contract
findings.description: The Logging__LogLevel__* verbosity mechanism works (live-verified) but is documented nowhere. runtime.md (AI-facing) documents the sink env var and 'operational logging goes to stderr'; the README and docs/ (consumer-facing, the surfaces a marketplace/registry installer actually reads) have no observability section — where logs land per host, how to raise verbosity, how to correlate, the server_info/heartbeat health route.
acceptance: A consumer-visible doc section answers: log destination per host, verbosity env vars (Logging__LogLevel__*), sink env var(s), correlation story, health route
runtime.md points at (or mirrors) the same contract without divergence
findings.suggested_approach: Add an Observability section to README or docs/stdio-client-integration.md using the A10 contract-table shape; cross-link from runtime.md.

findings.title: Fix corrupted env-var name 'n=stderr' in three published docs
evidence: grep: 'set `n=stderr`' in three docs; ai_docs/runtime.md:77 has the correct ROSLYNMCP_OBSERVABILITY_SINK
findings.description: Three consumer-facing docs instruct operators to 'set `n=stderr`' — a corrupted replacement of ROSLYNMCP_OBSERVABILITY_SINK (runtime.md retains the correct name). A consumer following these docs sets a nonsense env var and concludes the diagnostics feature is broken.
acceptance: All three docs name ROSLYNMCP_OBSERVABILITY_SINK=stderr; no literal 'n=' remnant remains repo-wide outside changelogs
findings.suggested_approach: Targeted text fix; add the correct name to the consumer-doc contract row's section so the two rows land coherently.

findings.title: Clean 7 dangling deps references to closed observability rows
evidence: backlog.mjs get: 'row not found' for both ids; git log: items deleted in PR #1253
findings.description: Six rows carry deps on mcp-logging-stderr-otel-migration and one on server-structured-observability-sink; both were closed in PR #1253 and no longer exist. Dangling deps mislead sweep planners into treating satisfiable rows as blocked.
acceptance: No deps cell references a non-existent row id (verified via backlog.mjs ids diff)
Rows whose only dep was a closed row show deps '—' or their remaining real deps
findings.suggested_approach: backlog.mjs update per affected row; consider whether backlog-lint should flag dangling deps (global tooling backlog, not this repo).
